correct: 'To leave us a remnant to escape, and to give us a nail in his holy place, that our God may lighten our eyes, and give us a little reviving in our bondage'
explanation: Ezra employs the architectural metaphor of a secure tent peg or structural peg ('a nail in his holy place') to portray God's fragile yet precious foothold of grace in the restored temple. Ezra 9:8 (KJV) - "And now for a little space grace hath been shewed from the LORD our God, to leave us a remnant to escape, and to give us a nail in his holy place, that our God may lighten our eyes, and give us a little reviving in our bondage."

question: How does Ezra describe the Persian imperial subjugation of Judah in his prayer of confession?
opt1: 'We are freemen under Persian law, and our kings reign with sovereign power over Judea'

opt3: 'We are wandering captives without a homeland, subject to the whims of the satraps of Media'

explanation: Ezra acknowledged their subordinate vassal status ('we were bondmen'), yet celebrated God's providential mercy in moving Persian monarchs to grant temple revival and defensive security ('a wall'). Ezra 9:9 (KJV) - "For we were bondmen; yet our God hath not forsaken us in our bondage, but hath extended mercy unto us in the sight of the kings of Persia, to give us a reviving, to set up the house of our God, and to repair the desolations thereof, and to give us a wall in Judah and in Jerusalem."

question: What profound recognition of divine leniency does Ezra confess regarding God's judgments against their past sins in Ezra 9:13?
opt1: 'And after all that is come upon us for our evil deeds, and for our great trespass, seeing that thou our God hast punished us less than our iniquities deserve, and hast given us such deliverance as this'

explanation: Ezra magnified God's mercy, candidly acknowledging that the severity of the exile was far milder than their staggering national sins deserved ('punished us less than our iniquities deserve'). Ezra 9:13 (KJV) - "And after all that is come upon us for our evil deeds, and for our great trespass, seeing that thou our God hast punished us less than our iniquities deserve, and hast given us such deliverance as this;"

question: What chilling theological question did Ezra ask concerning the inevitable consequence of repeating their ancestors' abominable intermarriages?
opt1: 'Will not the king of Persia take away our tax exemptions and deliver our children to Egypt?'

opt4: 'Can the temple of Mount Moriah endure if the sons of Aaron marry the daughters of Moab?'

explanation: Ezra warned that trampling divine grace by resuming covenant-breaking marriages invited total annihilation, leaving neither survivor nor escaping remnant. Ezra 9:14 (KJV) - "Should we again break thy commandments, and join in affinity with the people of these abominations? wouldest not thou be angry with us till thou hadst consumed us, so that there should be no remnant nor escaping?"

question: With what humble declaration of God's absolute righteousness and human defenselessness does Ezra close his prayer?

opt4: 'Hearken unto our weeping, O God of Abraham, and establish the work of our hands forever'
correct: 'O LORD God of Israel, thou art righteous: for we remain yet escaped, as it is this day: behold, we are before thee in our trespasses: for we cannot stand before thee because of this'
explanation: Ezra ended without presumptuous excuses: affirming God's spotless righteousness and confessing that guilty sinners possess no moral standing before Him. Ezra 9:15 (KJV) - "O LORD God of Israel, thou art righteous: for we remain yet escaped, as it is this day: behold, we are before thee in our trespasses: for we cannot stand before thee because of this."

question: What spontaneous national gathering occurred as Ezra wept and prayed prostrate before the house of God?

opt4: The Persian satrap dispatched twenty horsemen to disperse the weeping crowd

Ezra 10:1 (KJV) - "Now when Ezra had prayed, and when he had confessed, weeping and casting himself down before the house of God, there assembled unto him out of Israel a very great congregation of men and women and children: for the people wept very sore."

question: Which leader stepped forward to propose a radical covenant solution, uttering the famous words, 'Yet now there is hope in Israel concerning this thing'?

question: Where did Ezra retreat to fast and mourn without bread or water after administering the oath to the leadership?

question: Within how many days were all Judean citizens commanded to assemble in Jerusalem, and what severe dual penalty was threatened for non-compliance?

question: What weather and physical conditions attended the national assembly sitting in the temple square on the twentieth day of the ninth month (Chisleu)?

It was the ninth month, on the twentieth day of the month; and all the people sat in the street of the house of God, trembling because of this matter, and for the great rain."

question: What practical procedural counter-proposal did the shivering congregation present to Ezra in Ezra 10:13-14?
